🧳 External / portable drive · 🔍 Not detected / not showing up

External Hard Drive Not Showing Up or Detected

An external drive has a hard drive inside plus a small bridge board that turns USB into the drive's own connection. The fault could be the cable, the port, the bridge board, or the drive itself. Start with cheap, safe checks.

3/5 · Take care
Success odds: Varies

Cable and software checks are safe, but taking the drive out of its case can lock encrypted data or damage it.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Do not format or initialize the drive if the computer offers to. That can erase the data.
  • Do not keep plugging and unplugging if you hear clicking or the drive feels hot. That adds wear.
  • Do not open the drive's case yet. Many portable drives are encrypted or have USB soldered to the drive, so removing it can make data unreadable.

🧑‍🔧 When to call a pro

If it is not detected on any computer with a good cable, or it is a soldered or encrypted portable model with important data, stop and consider a professional.

Questions people ask

Can I just take the drive out and plug it into my computer?

Sometimes, but not always. Some portables have no standard SATA port, and some encrypt data using the original enclosure's board, so the data may look blank outside it.

How do I tell a bad enclosure from a bad drive?

If the drive spins and sounds normal but no disk appears on any computer, the bridge board may be bad. Clicking, grinding or silence points to the drive itself.

Should I format it when Windows asks?

No. Formatting can erase the data you want to save. Use TestDisk first.
